skill.name: research-driven-planning
skill.description: Guides structured software planning through requirements capture, evidence collection, task decomposition, and repeated pre-mortem risk review. It produces planning artifacts for implementation handoff and future feedback loops.
skill.summary: Plan complex software work with research evidence, structured tasks, and iterative risk review.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, JavaScript templates, and fixed project artifact paths. The real risks are external command execution through npx claude-flow@alpha and command substitutions that persist project contents into Claude Flow memory. No evidence found for prompt injection, credential theft, destructive file access, or malicious reconnaissance instructions.

remediation.suggestion: Pin claude-flow to a reviewed version, document the expected package source, and require user confirmation before any npx execution.

remediation.issue: Project data stored through memory commands
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before storing SPEC.md or planning packages, and add guidance to redact secrets and confidential business data.

remediation.issue: Generated files are written into project paths
remediation.suggestion: Create the artifact directories explicitly, use fixed output paths only, and state which files may be overwritten.

actual_capabilities: Guides creation of SPEC.md with requirements, constraints, and success criteria.
Defines a six-agent research workflow for evidence gathering and technology comparison.
Transforms specifications into an enhanced implementation plan with risks and dependencies.
Runs iterative pre-mortem review with consensus and failure-confidence checks.
Packages planning outputs for implementation handoff through files and memory namespaces.
limitations: Requires clear project goals, constraints, and success criteria from the user.
Depends on Claude Flow commands and agent workflows that may not exist in every environment.
Takes more time than direct implementation and may be too heavy for small fixes.
Confidence scores depend on the quality and freshness of collected evidence.

use_cases.title: Clarify Feature Scope
use_cases.description: Turn a broad product idea into requirements, constraints, success criteria, and explicit exclusions.

use_cases.title: Choose a Technical Approach
use_cases.description: Compare libraries, patterns, and platform choices using evidence before committing to implementation.

use_cases.title: Review Build Risk Early
use_cases.description: Identify failure modes, mitigation strategies, and handoff risks before a development swarm starts.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Planning Pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use research-driven-planning for this feature: [feature]. Capture requirements, constraints, success criteria, and out-of-scope items before research.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Implementation Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use research-driven-planning to compare approaches for [problem]. Include evidence sources, security tradeoffs, reliability risks, and a recommended path.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Pre-Mortem
prompt_templates.prompt: Use research-driven-planning to run a pre-mortem for this plan: [plan summary]. Identify likely failures, root causes, mitigations, and acceptance checks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Implementation Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced handoff to an implementation workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use research-driven-planning to create a handoff package for Loop 2. Include validated requirements, research-backed tasks, risk mitigations, and readiness criteria.

output_examples.input: Plan authentication for an Express and PostgreSQL product with role-based access and two-factor authentication.
output: A requirements summary covering login, refresh tokens, roles, password reset, and two-factor authentication.
Research-backed recommendations for token storage, password hashing, rate limits, and audit logging.
A risk register with mitigations for account takeover, token leakage, migration failure, and latency targets.

output_examples.input: Compare payment provider options before building a billing workflow.
output: A ranked provider comparison using reliability, compliance, integration cost, and developer experience.
A task plan with dependencies for checkout, webhooks, invoice handling, and failure recovery.
A pre-mortem summary covering duplicate charges, webhook replay, reconciliation gaps, and rollback plans.

output_examples.input: Prepare a handoff package for a large refactor with unknown regression risk.
output: A scoped specification with migration goals, excluded changes, and measurable success criteria.
Evidence from similar refactors and recommended sequencing for low-risk delivery.
A Loop 2 readiness summary with artifacts, namespaces, validation checks, and unresolved risks.

best_practices: Provide constraints, current architecture, and success metrics before starting research.
Review evidence quality and source freshness before accepting any recommendation.
Use the pre-mortem output to change the plan, not only to document risks.
anti_patterns: Using this workflow for urgent hotfixes or small edits that do not need research.
Treating consensus scores as proof when evidence sources are weak or outdated.
Handing off a plan before unresolved critical risks have owners and mitigations.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a specification, research synthesis, enhanced task plan, pre-mortem results, and an implementation handoff package.

faq.question: Is this skill only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: It is written for Claude and Claude Code workflows, but the planning method can inform Codex-assisted work too.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it for trivial changes, emergency fixes, or work where the approach is already proven and low risk.

faq.question: Does it perform research automatically?
faq.answer: It defines agent research steps and prompts. Actual research depends on the tools and network access available in your environment.

faq.question: Can it guarantee less than three percent failure risk?
faq.answer: No. The threshold is a planning target, not a guarantee. It depends on evidence quality and honest risk review.

faq.question: What security precautions should I take?
faq.answer: Review external commands before running them, pin third-party tools, and avoid storing secrets in generated planning artifacts.
